chapter: Jelly Roll Morton and other records
title: Using the mute: Oliver's effect he could not match
summary: On the Morton records he played open horn; he never mastered mute work like Oliver, who remained his favorite.

bands.name: Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: you ever use a mute in those days much? Like on those jelly records? Did you? Let's see.
I don't think we used mute much with jelly. I think mostly it was open horn. I think mostly it was open horn.
Did you ever do much mute work otherwise?

No, no, I never did do. Because I couldn't ever get that effect like Joe did. Like Joe did. I tried it. I wanted two tunes there. I can't think of what it was. What was that? Oh, God, we used a single-less one or something. I used to try to use that, but I couldn't handle that pretty well. But I couldn't handle that mute like Joe. I always was one like to use that mute, but I could never get that effect like Joe. Well, Joe had the ideas he had, you know, playing this. I just didn't have. But Joe was my favorite trumpet playing that type of music.
